candidates.angle: bhavitavya, appointed, reveals Arjuna sees himself as a puppet
candidates.evidence: बलात् इव नियोजितः (as if appointed by force)

candidates.angle: Arjuna names the self as the one who does wrong
Arjuna asks what power pushes a person against their will

angle_en: bhavitavya: the word that shows Arjuna feels like a puppet
angle_hi: bhavitavya: शब्द जो दिखाता है अर्जुन स्वयं को कठपुतली समझते हैं

en.intro: Krishna has just told Arjuna to do his own duty, so Arjuna pushes back, asking what power moves a person against their own will.
en.notice: The word bhavitavya means appointed, and Arjuna uses it to describe himself. He is saying he feels like a puppet, driven by some outside force to do wrong, even though he does not want to.
en.next: Krishna answers by naming desire as the force that drives a person into anger and destruction.
en.meaning: Arjuna says: O descendant of the Vrishni clan, what drives a person to commit wrongdoing, even unwillingly, as if forced?

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी अर्जुन से अपना कर्तव्य निभाने को कहा है, इसलिए अर्जुन पूछते हैं कि वह कौन सी शक्ति है जो मनुष्य को उसकी इच्छा के विरुद्ध धकेलती है।
hi.meaning: अर्जुन पूछते हैं, हे वार्ष्णेय, फिर कौन सी शक्ति मनुष्य को न चाहते हुए भी पाप करने पर विवश करती है, मानो कोई उसे ज़बरदस्ती इसमें लगा रहा हो।
hi.notice: बलात् इव नियोजितः का अर्थ है मानो बलपूर्वक नियुक्त। अर्जुन स्वयं को एक कठपुतली की तरह महसूस कर रहे हैं जिसे कोई बाहरी शक्ति गलत काम करने के लिए विवश कर रही है, जबकि वह स्वयं यह नहीं चाहते।
hi.next: कृष्ण इसका उत्तर देते हुए कहते हैं कि काम ही वह शक्ति है जो मनुष्य को क्रोध और विनाश की ओर ले जाती है।

en.intro: Krishna has just told Arjuna to do his own duty, so Arjuna pushes back, asking what power moves a person against their own will.
en.body: Arjuna says: O descendant of the Vrishni clan, what drives a person to commit wrongdoing, even unwillingly, as if forced? The word bhavitavya means appointed, and Arjuna uses it to describe himself. He is saying he feels like a puppet, driven by some outside force to do wrong, even though he does not want to. Krishna answers by naming desire as the force that drives a person into anger and destruction.
